title: Legacy disciplinary and attendance point framework
summary: Undated/legacy discipline materials document earlier point-based escalation examples and a blank violation matrix. Their attendance thresholds are superseded by the current December 15, 2025 handbook's six-point attendance system and current Group A-D disciplinary guidelines.

claims.claim: An undated discipline example document shows two parallel point-threshold ladders: 2/4/6/8/10 points mapped to verbal/written/final/suspension/discharge, and 5/7/10/15/18-20 points mapped to verbal/WW1/WW2/final warning/termination.

evidence.note: The source does not identify what distinguishes the two side-by-side ladders.

claims.claim: The same source assigns 1/2 point to tardiness, 1 point to unexcused absences, and an extra 1/2 point for failing to give notice.
The legacy source says satisfactory performance for one year may allow new violations to be treated as first occurrences, while past discipline may still be considered.
The legacy source explicitly states progressive discipline is discretionary and a first offense may justify discharge in some circumstances.

evidence.note: This is consistent with the later handbook discretion language.

claims.claim: A separate legacy workbook is structured as a violation matrix with 1st-, 2nd-, and 3rd-offense point/date columns and includes operational violations spanning attendance, dress code, safety, billing, client information, trip processing, denials, prior authorization, eligibility, breaks, cell phones, and work rules; the supplied point/date assessment cells are blank.

evidence.note: The workbook was converted and inspected; the point/date assessment columns contain no values in the supplied copy.

claims.claim: The December 15, 2025 handbook uses a different attendance-point system: partial-day points of 1/4, 1/2 or 1 point; written warning at 2 points, three-day unpaid suspension at 4 points, and termination at 6 points. This supersedes the legacy 10-point attendance examples for current use.

The December 15, 2025 handbook provides the current Group A-D disciplinary guideline matrix and expressly treats it as suggested guidance subject to supervisor determination, superseding the legacy unlabeled point matrices as the current general discipline reference.

Separate restricted 2012 attendance memos explicitly reference a 9-point suspension level and a 10-point termination level, providing corroborated historical evidence of an attendance-point ladder distinct from the unlabeled point examples preserved elsewhere.

evidence.note: Employee identity and case facts excluded.
Employee identity and case facts excluded.

claims.claim: Historical case evidence also shows attendance points were discussed separately from FMLA-protected time, supporting the interpretation that protected FMLA absences were not simply treated as ordinary attendance-point events.

evidence.note: The source distinguishes remaining FMLA time from non-FMLA absences/tardiness.

steps: Identify the violation and prior offense history.
Use the applicable historical point/escalation framework only when its date, scope, and authority are established.
Apply management discretion allowed by the governing policy.
decisions: Which historical framework applied to the employee/job/incident date?
Whether the infraction warrants skipping progressive steps.
deadlines: One legacy example references a 12-month period and satisfactory record for one year.
exceptions: First-offense discharge may be appropriate under certain circumstances according to the legacy example.
controls: Do not combine the two point ladders or infer their scope without corroborating evidence.
The Disciplinary steps workbook is a blank historical matrix/template; do not infer point values from its column headings.
Do not merge historical point ladders into one synthetic policy; preserve each dated/undated framework until its scope and supersession are established.
Protected-leave status must be resolved before applying attendance-point logic.
unresolved_questions: What date/version and employee population did each of the two legacy point ladders govern?
What historical date/version and employee population did each of the two unlabeled legacy point ladders govern before the current handbook system?
How did the 2012 9-point suspension / 10-point termination attendance ladder relate to the two unlabeled point ladders in the undated Disciplinary Examples document?
What attendance events counted as points, what events reduced or expired points, and how were protected FMLA/other protected absences excluded?
automation_candidates: Policy-version-aware discipline reference that requires the incident date/employee class before surfacing any point matrix.

provenance.notes: Undated legacy workbook; deterministically inspected after XLS conversion. Violation labels are populated, but point/date assessment cells are blank.
Current handbook resolves current-use status of legacy point references.
